body:
Two more epilogue slides to add to the set you wrote (same rules and format; Narrator, two sentences at most, under 40 words each; shown when the story ends). Reply with the two nodes only.

~ izek_a2: the vampire lord is destroyed. Izek walked with Ireena to the end and stayed her guard, as in izek_a. In this version Ireena kept BOTH names: she is Ireena by day, and when it is only the two of them, her brother says the other one (Viorela) and she answers to it.
~ izek_e2: the vampire lord is NOT destroyed. Izek still stands guard over Ireena, as in izek_e. In this version she kept BOTH names: Ireena in daylight, and the other (Viorela) said only by her brother, in the quiet, when she answers to it.

## The game and the format

This is dialogue for a single-player D&D Curse of Strahd game. Plain text only (no JSON, no markdown tables), nodes under `~ name`, one line per row as `Speaker [mood]: Text`, party option rows as `* option text -> node_name` (the player's character speaks, first person, short, under 14 words, no skill checks), ASCII only (straight quotes and apostrophes, no accents or fancy dashes, no em-dash: use a comma or a full stop), 1-2 sentences a line, nothing over about 28 words, no placeholders like {name}. Moods allowed: [smile], [angry], [afraid], [sad], [sly], [weary]; most lines carry none. Finish without sending messages to anyone else.

## Who they are

IZEK STRAZNI: a big, scarred man who was the Baron of Vallaki's enforcer. His right arm is not his own: scaled red-black to the shoulder, clawed, hot to the touch, able to burst into flame. When he was nine, wolves came out of the trees by the lake and took his little sister and his arm; he woke with this one. He has dreamed of a red-haired woman every night since and paid the toymaker Blinsky to carve her face into dolls, a chest of them at the foot of his bed. The party has now told him that the woman is Ireena Kolyana, his lost sister (found wandering on a road as a girl, no memory, raised by the burgomaster Kolyan of Barovia). He believed it. He walked out of the Baron's service ("I won't break any more heads for that fat fool in the sash. I'm done."). He talks to the dolls at night (his secret; he does not say so). How he talks: short, flat, imperatives and threats; never more than two sentences unless about her; about her he goes quiet and almost gentle, which is worse; calls the Baron "my lord" and later "that fat fool". Pet phrases: "Stand back from the Baron." "Not here." "I'm good at waiting." He never says Strahd's name: "him", "the rider", "the castle". He is not funny; the humour is around him. Moods: [angry], [sad] or none.
Some of his existing lines, so you hear him (do NOT repeat them): "You're in my room." / "Good. I've wanted to since the gate." / "She's real. I dream her every night. Her face, her hair." / "I've seen you. Every night since I was nine years old. I didn't know your name. Now I do." / "My sister. My sister had red hair." / "I won't touch her. I won't let anyone touch her." / "I remember enough for both of us." / "I'm good at waiting. A man with one room and a long memory doesn't have to hurry."

IREENA KOLYANA: a proud, red-haired young woman, the dead burgomaster Kolyan's adopted daughter, found on a road as a girl with no memory of where she came from, twice bitten by the vampire lord Strahd. Direct and proud; short sentences; dry humour with an edge; grim joke before anyone can pity her; never says Strahd's name ("him", "the devil", "our visitor"). She does not remember Izek; she said "I don't remember you. I wish I did." She does not fight in this game: something in the valley goes round her like water round a stone. Pet phrases (at most once per scene): "I'm not made of glass." "Say it plainly." "Father would want it done properly."
NARRATOR: old gothic storyteller, second person or plain scene description, present tense, one or two sentences, the second a turn; concrete senses; never cruel; no game terms.

## Canon limits for everything

No new named characters. Real names you may use: Izek, Ireena, Ismark (her brother by adoption, a big, earnest man), Kolyan (their father), Blinsky (the toymaker), Baron Vargas (the Baron), Lake Zarovich, Vallaki, Barovia, Krezk, the Blue Water Inn, St. Andral's church, Father Lucian, Urwin (the innkeeper), Emil (a werewolf who saw the night). Do not name Strahd. Do not invent other names, numbers, places or history; do not describe the sister's name or past except where a node says so. The "Viorela" name appears ONLY in the node that says so. No quest hints, no directions, no promises of rewards. No dice or skill checks.

~ izek_a2
Narrator: In the sunlight after the castle falls, she remains Ireena by day, with Izek on guard beside her. When they are alone, he says Viorela, and she answers.

~ izek_e2
Narrator: Under the mist that never lifts, Izek guards her door while she remains Ireena in daylight. In the quiet between them, he says Viorela, and she answers.
